(SCCH-24)
 Presided Over by Smt. Roopashri, B.Com., LL.B.,
 XXII ADDL., SCJ & ACJM,
 MEMBER - MACT,
 BENGALURU.
Dated:- This the 7th day of September 2024

Petitioner H.R Chandrashekar,
 S/o Rajashekhar  Aged about 41 years,
 R/at Ambikanagara,
 Arasinakunte,
 Bangalore Rural  Pin -562123.
 (By Sri.Krishnamurthy, Advocate)

-VERSUS-  Respondent The Managing Director,
 K.S.R.T.C Depot,

Bengaluru Central Office,
 K.H road, Shanthinagar,
Bengaluru -560027.

(RC owner of KSRTC bus bearing  Reg.No.KA-57-F-4282)
 (By Smt. Savitha K R, Advocate)
 SCCH-24 2 MVC 2502/2023  :J U D G M E N T:

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
2.

The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 16-03-2023 at about 10-15 a.m., the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing No.KA-01-HL- 0096 from Bengaluru -Tumkur NH-48 service road.

When he reached near Haliday Hotel, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore District, at that time the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Bus bearing Reg No.KA-57-F-4282 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Deo moped, result of which the Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
1
petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Nelamangala Government Hospital wherein primary treatment was given.

Due to severe pain the petitioner has taken treatment at Sree Siddhartha Hospital,
Tumkur as an inpatient from 20-03- 2023 to 28-03-2023 and underwent surgery.
The petitioner is still taking follow up treatment and so far he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was driver by profession and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

3. Respondent- the RC owner of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-4282 has filed written statement and contended that on 16-03-2023 the offending bus was being operated on its schedule trip from Bangalore to Y N Hoskote.

The said bus was proceeding on NH -48 service road near Nelamangala in front of Holiday Hotel, at that time the petitioner came in a two wheeler from behind riding the same in a rash and negligent manner and tried to over take the bus from left side and as there was gravel (jally) stones, due to over speed the petitioner lost control over his two wheeler and fell down on the road.
Observing the same the driver of bus stopped the bus and on humanitarian ground shifted the petitioner to the Nelamangala Government Hospital.
It is submitted by the respondent that rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner itself is the sole cause for accident; hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.
04. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 16-03-2023 at about 10-15 am., near Holiday Hotel, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F- 4282?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3
. What order or award?

5. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked in all seventeen documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.
6.
On the hand, the respondent examined its driver as R.W.1 and got marked Postal acknowledgment as Ex.R1.

Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
2
7. Heard arguments of the petitioner and respondent.
Perused the material placed on record.

08. My findings on the above-referred Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1:- In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2:- In Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3:-

As per the final order,
 for the following.

:REASONS:
9. Issue No.1:

- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, PW1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 16-03-2023 at about 10-15 a.m. when the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing No.KA-01- HL-0096 from Bengaluru -Tumkur NH-48 service road and when he reached near Holiday Hotel, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore District, at that time the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Bus bearing Reg No.KA-57-F-4282 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Deo moped, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

10. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon the Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint,
spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.
11.

In order to negative the claim of the petitioner and to prove that no accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus, the driver of the said bus has been examined as Rw1 and through him got marked postal acknowledgment at Ex.R1.

It is categorically contended both in the written statement and in the evidence of Rw1 that, on the stated date the driver of offending vehicle was on a schedule trip from Bangalore to Y N Hoskote and while he was so proceeding near Nelamangala in front of Holiday Hotel, at that time the petitioner came in a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-01- HL-0096 from behind riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, tried to over take the bus from left side and as there was gravel (jally) stones, due to over speed he lost control over his motorcycle and fell on the road and sustained injuries.
12.

The learned counsel for the respondent vehemently submitted that there is delay of three days in taking treatment at Siddhartha Hospital and that the accident in question has not occurred in the manner stated by the petitioner and that if really offending vehicle has hit against the motorcycle from behind, then damages would have been caused to the motorcycle on its rear side and on the offending vehicle on its front side , but in the IMV report there is mention about damage caused on the front portion of the motorcycle and rear portion of the offending vehicle.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for respondent that the petitioner has not produced driving license, hence by driving the motorcycle without having driving license the petitioner too has contributed negligence.

13. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent, if the materials placed on record are Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
3 perused, it is true that the petitioner has not produced original driving licence but has produced notarized copy of the driving licence.
As per the said document the driving licence of the petitioner was in force as on the date of accident.
It is deposed by PW.1 that he has lost his driving licence hence unable to produce the original driving licence.
It is relevant to state here that along with the notarized copy of driving licence at Ex.P9, the petitioner has produced the Xerox copy of lost article report.
As per the said document the petitioner has lost his original driving licence during the year 2021 and to that effect he has lodged complaint .

Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of discussion that as on the date of accident the petitioner had no driving licence, then also unless the rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner is proved on mere ground that the petitioner had no driving licence negligence cannot be attributed against the petitioner .

14. So far as the rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent is concerned, as per the case of the petitioner, at the time of accident he was proceeding in two wheeler in Bangalore -Tumkur road, the offending vehicle which came from behind the two wheeler of the petitioner hit against his vehicle.

15. Per contra, it is the defence of the respondent that the petitioner by riding his vehicle from behind the offending vehicle tried to overtake the offending vehicle from the left side and lost control over the vehicle and fell on the jally stone and sustained injuries.
16. If the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 26 feet and the accident in question has occurred at a distance of 5 feet from the left edge of tar road.

When offending vehicle is a heavy vehicle compared to two wheeler the driver of the offending vehicle ought to have drive his vehicle by leaving sufficient space in the left side for the user of two wheeler .
Further none of the police document discloses the fact of existence of any jally heap near the spot of accident and also the fact of petitioner overtook the offending vehicle from left side.

The mere fact that the front portion of the motorcycle got damaged instead on the rear side, on that ground alone the court cannot come to the conclusion that the offending vehicle did not hit against to the two wheeler .

It is deposed by PW.1 that the offending vehicle which came from behind of his vehicle touched his vehicle on its rear side result of which he fell on the road along with motorcycle and sustained injury and simultaneously his vehicle is also got damaged.
When offending vehicle is coming from behind the two wheeler, had the driver of offending vehicle maintained minimum distance this accident could have been avoided.
It is true that the driver of offending vehicle has led his evidence as RW.1 and deposed about the manner of accident.
But if really the accident in question has occurred in the manner stated by the RW.1 then nothing prevented the Rw1 from lodging complaint against the petitioner.
But he has not taken any such steps at an earliest point of time.
Hence, materials placed on record prove that the driver of offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2 :- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.

As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P4 and examined MRD of Sri Siddaratha Medical College by name Ramakrishnappa K and through him produced discharge summary, IP bills, case sheet and x- rays as per Ex.P10 to Ex.P13.

On going through the Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
4 medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 20-03-2023 to 28-03-2023 at Sree Siddharatha Hospital for a period of 9 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained four injuries which are grievous in nature.
18. Dr.Ramesh B -Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore has given evidence as Pw3.
Through him OPD and x-ray film are marked at Ex.P.14 and P.15.
The Pw3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner radiological for assessment of disability.

Pw.3 further deposed that the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of the right upper limb at 39% and whole body physical disability at 13%, that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant.
19. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, and this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
20. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained four grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
21. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced 47 medical bill for Rs.60,108/- and Rs.13,750/- as per Ex.P.6 and Ex.P11.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.73,858/- under the head medical expenses.
22. It is stated that petitioner was 41 years and he was working as car driver and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
23.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient at Sree Siddharatha Hospital, Tumkur.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for two months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
24. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 9 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.

He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2023.
25.
So far as the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner is concerned, if the evidence of PW.3 is carefully perused, admittedly PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
5
As per the evidence of PW.3 there is mal-union of fracture.

The learned counsel for respondent by cross examining the PW.1 so also during the course of argument has vehemently stated that if petitioner had taken treatment at an earliest time the fracture would not be mal-united.
The PW.3 has denied the said fact and deposed that the delayed treatment may be one of the reason for mal union but it may not be the sole cause for mal - union .
If the evidence of PW.1 is perused, soon after the accident he has taken treatment at Anekal Government Hospital.
Due to financial crisis he got discharged from the said hospital on the same date of admission itself.
As he suffered pain in the injuries after three days of the accident he got admitted at Siddhartha Hospital and taken treatment as inpatient for 9 days and underwent surgery.
Hence, considering the aforesaid fact this court inclines to take the disability of petitioner on whole body at 10% instead of 13%.
26. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 41 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P8/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01-01-1982 that means he was aged 41 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 41 years.

27. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/- p.m and if 10% of loss of earning capacity is considered as loss of earning capacity and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 41 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

So by applying the multiplier '14'
the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.2,60,400/-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,60,400/- (i.e., 15,500 x10% x 14 x12 ) towards future loss of income due to disability.
28. As per the evidence of Pw3, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant.
If the medical records of the petitioner are perused, he has taken treatment for a period of 9 days and underwent surgery for fixation of implant and for other injuries.
For 9 days of treatment as inpatient the petitioner had incurred only sum of Rs.73,858/-.

Hence this court inclines to award compensation under the head future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.25,000/-.
29.
The petitioner at his age of 41 years has suffered grievous injuries and permanent disability of 10%.
Hence it may cause some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence this court inclines to award sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl.
No Heads Amount Rs.
1 . Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 60,000/-

2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food

3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 31,000/-
 laid up period 4. Loss of Future Income Rs.2,60,400/-

5 . Medical expenses Rs. 73,858/-
Chandrashekar H.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181787572/
6 6.

Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-
7. loss of comfort and amenities Rs. 20,000/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,95,258/- (Rupees Four Lakh Ninety Five Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Eight only)
30.
As regarding liability is concerned, the Respondent being the RC owner cum insured of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 are answered in partly affirmative.
31. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total  compensation of Rs.4,95,258/- + cost of Rs.250/- imposed vide order date 21-06-2024.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.4,95,508/- (Rupees Four Lakh Ninety Five Thousand Five Hundred Eight only)

After deducting cost of Rs.250/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.25,000/- balance sum of Rs.4,70,258/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
